Discern

/dih-SURN/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Discern means to perceive or recognize something, especially something subtle or hard to notice

Standing on the dark porch, Leo could barely discern the outline of the mountains against the night sky.

Worked Example

An art restorer examined the painting under a bright lamp for nearly an hour. Slowly she began to discern tiny irregularities in the brushstrokes, details invisible to a casual viewer, that revealed the canvas was a forgery.

The restorer perceives something subtle only through careful, sustained attention, which is the core of discern: detecting what is not immediately obvious.

How Discern Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

perceive

perceive: to become aware of through the senses or mind

detect

detect: to discover the presence of something

distinguish

distinguish: to recognize as different or separate

Antonyms

overlook

overlook: to fail to notice

miss

miss: to not see or catch something

How Strong Is It? — notice → discern → scrutinize

notice vs. discern

notice vs. discern: Notice describes perception that simply happens to you, while discern suggests deliberate effort to pick out something subtle.

scrutinize vs. discern

scrutinize vs. discern: Discern is gentler than scrutinize, which means to examine something intensely and critically, inch by inch.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart (not negation in this word)

Root — cern

Root — cern: to sift, separate, distinguish (Latin cernere)

Put it together

Put it together: Watch out: in this word dis- means 'apart,' not 'not' or 'opposite of,' even though that is this unit's headline pattern. Discern comes from dis- (apart) plus Latin cernere (to sift, to separate), literally 'to sift apart,' which is why it means telling things apart clearly.

Use the root in a new word: discrete

Use the root in a new word: discrete: The course is divided into five discrete units, each one fully separate from the others.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal

Discern suits careful, effortful perception of subtle things; when something is obvious, plain words like notice or tell sound more natural. Also watch a classic confusable: discern (to perceive or detect) is unrelated to discreet (careful and tactful about what you say or do), despite the similar look and sound.
